In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymer adsorbs to the surfactant membrane and the adsorption increases with increasing C(PEG).
PEG adsorbing into surfactant membranes slows down the membrane dynamics, but the polymer does not affect the membrane elasticity in the range of polymer concentrations investigated.
the effect of PEG on the membrane elasticity is a combination of the effects of adsorption and of penetration of the polymer in the membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polymer slows down the membrane dynamics and penetrates into the membrane, which results in the increase in the membrane bending modulus.
the bending modulus of the SDS membranes is not only increased by the presence of polymer but also by the penetration of the polymer into the bilayers.
the polymer, in addition to the adsorption at the membrane surface, interacts with the surfactant molecules in the bilayer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DLS can be used as a powerful tool to investigate the effect of polymers on the elasticity of membranes.
the bending modulus of surfactant bilayer is a function of the polymer concentration, and this dependence is not necessarily monotonic.
the bending elastic modulus of the surfactants membranes is not a constant but depends on the polymer concentration, which in turn depends on the membrane composition.
